summary: This bill expands eligibility for special overtime pay to U.S. Border Patrol agents classified from grade GS-12 through GS-15, rather than limiting it to only those at grade GS-12.

scores.thoughts: This bill expands eligibility for special overtime pay to a broader range of Border Patrol agents, which would likely lead to increased government expenditures for agent salaries and benefits. This directly increases government spending.

The bill aims to improve retention of Border Patrol supervisors by expanding overtime pay eligibility, which is intended to strengthen border security operations. This directly supports the goal of securing borders.

By enhancing the compensation structure for Border Patrol agents, the bill indirectly supports law enforcement efforts at the border, which falls under the broader umbrella of stricter justice and stronger policing.

The bill expands eligibility for special overtime pay to Border Patrol supervisors (GS-13 through GS-15), modestly increasing federal personnel expenditures without any offsetting revenue provisions. Its core purpose is retention incentives, not fiscal balance, so the effect on deficits is real but peripheral.
